root_cause.text: The RDMA/iwcm subsystem incorrectly maintained a separate per-CM-ID `work_list` of `struct iwcm_work` objects and reused embedded `work_struct`s from a free list, so `cm_work_handler()` could free and reinitialize an entry while its workqueue item was still pending, causing double-queued work and list corruption.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `work_list` from `struct iwcm_id_private`/`struct iwcm_work`, deletes the `list_add_tail()` and `while (!list_empty(&cm_id_priv->work_list))` processing in `cm_event_handler()`/`cm_work_handler()`, and the commit message explicitly says `queue_work()` was called unconditionally on unique free-list entries, letting a single run process item N+1 while its actual workqueue entry was still queued and then reused with `INIT_WORK()`, leading to `list_del corruption`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unused `list` linkage from `iwcm_work` to simplify the structure definition.
intent_record.what: The `struct iwcm_work` definition has one field removed: the `struct list_head list;` member was deleted, while the other members (`work`, `cm_id`, `event`, and `free_list`) remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: This changes the in-memory layout of `iwcm_work` so objects of this type no longer carry an embedded list node named `list`. At runtime, code can no longer rely on that member for linking `iwcm_work` instances into a list, which suggests the structure is no longer intended to be used in that way.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove redundant list-head initialization from alloc_work_entries().
intent_record.what: The call to INIT_LIST_HEAD(&work->list) was removed from alloc_work_entries() before put_work(work) is called.
intent_record.how: Work entries are now passed to put_work() without explicitly initializing their list head in this function, so list initialization must be handled elsewhere or is no longer needed at this point.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the invalid BUG_ON assertion during CM ID dereference so the object can be freed without a kernel panic.
intent_record.what: The `BUG_ON(!list_empty(&cm_id_priv->work_list));` check was removed from `iwcm_deref_id()`, so when the refcount reaches zero the function now directly calls `free_cm_id(cm_id_priv)` without asserting that `work_list` is empty.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code no longer crashes the kernel if `cm_id_priv->work_list` is non-empty when the last reference is dropped. This removes a hard failure path and allows cleanup to proceed even if pending work items remain associated with the object.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove redundant `work_list` initialization from CM ID creation.
intent_record.what: The call to `INIT_LIST_HEAD(&cm_id_priv->work_list);` was removed from `iw_create_cm_id()`, while `INIT_LIST_HEAD(&cm_id_priv->work_free_list);` remains unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the `work_list` member is no longer explicitly initialized as an empty list at CM ID creation time. This changes the object initialization sequence and may rely on `work_list` being initialized elsewhere or being unused in this path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reword and reflow the `cm_work_handler()` comment for clarity without changing behavior.
intent_record.what: The block comment above `cm_work_handler()` was reworded: it now says "Process events for the cm_id" instead of "Process events on the work_list for the cm_id," and the surrounding explanatory lines were reflowed with minor line-wrapping changes. No executable code was changed.
intent_record.how: This does not change runtime behavior; it only updates documentation to describe the handler more generally and improves comment readability.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify the CM work handler to process one queued event per invocation instead of iterating through the entire work list.
intent_record.what: The work handler was changed from looping over and processing every entry in cm_id_priv->work_list to handling only a single work item: the code that removed the first list entry, iterated over the list, and re-locked the spinlock was deleted, and the remaining logic now just uses the current work item's event, releases it, unlocks, processes that one event, and dereferences the cm_id once.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the handler no longer drains the entire queued event list in one invocation; instead it processes only one queued event per call. This changes event handling from batch processing under a loop to single-event processing, which can affect ordering/latency and relies on the work scheduling path to invoke the handler again for remaining queued events.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop adding the work item to `cm_id_priv->work_list` before queuing it, correcting CM event work handling.
intent_record.what: The call to `list_add_tail(&work->list, &cm_id_priv->work_list);` was removed from `cm_event_handler()`, while `refcount_inc(&cm_id_priv->refcount);` and `queue_work(iwcm_wq, &work->work);` remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, work items are no longer explicitly inserted into `cm_id_priv->work_list` before being queued. This changes the handling of queued CM events by eliminating the list linkage step, which can prevent duplicate or unnecessary list management for the work item.

intent_record.what: The `work_list` field was removed from the `struct iwcm_id_private` definition, leaving the other members unchanged.
intent_record.how: This changes the in-memory layout of `iwcm_id_private` and eliminates the stored list head that was previously part of each instance. At runtime, code can no longer rely on this per-object `work_list` member being present for queueing or tracking work items.

In `cm_event_handler()` it does `work = get_work(cm_id_priv);`, initializes the embedded work item with `INIT_WORK(&work->work, cm_work_handler, work);`, and queues it only when `list_empty(&cm_id_priv->work_list)` is true.     RDMA/iwcm: Simplify cm_event_handler()

bic_trace_step.reason: Yes, the snippet is enough to assess the issue because it shows the exact work-queue enqueue logic in cm_event_handler(). The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is present: the code maintains a per-CM-ID work_list and uses an embedded work_struct, adding every new work item with `list_add_tail(&work->list, &cm_id_priv->work_list);` and then queuing it with `queue_work(iwcm_wq, &work->work);`. This commit explicitly changes the behavior from conditional queuing (`if (list_empty(...)) { ... queue_work(...); } else ...`) to unconditional queuing, which means the function no longer contains the prior safety check that prevented multiple queued items on the same list. The fix for the historical bug would be to remove the problematic separate list/reuse pattern or otherwise ensure a work item cannot be reinitialized while pending; that is not present here. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not yet present in this commit.
